The asn1parse-test binary also crashes on ALL inputs, even empty. So both the asn1-test and asn1parse-test binaries crash on any input locally. This is a build/environment issue with the local binaries, not the actual vulnerability.

Wait, but earlier when I ran `echo "test" | ./fuzz/asn1parse-test 2>&1 | head -3; echo "rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"`, it returned rc=0. Let me re-check. Oh, the `head -3` was consuming the output and `PIPESTATUS[0]` was the exit of the test binary. But it showed rc=0. That's contradictory with the current result.

Wait, let me re-check. Earlier I ran:
```
echo "test" | ./fuzz/$t 2>&1 | head -3; echo "rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
```
And it showed rc=0 for asn1parse-test. But now `echo -n "test" | ./fuzz/asn1parse-test` gives rc=139. 

The difference: earlier I used `echo "test"` (with newline) and piped through `head -3`. Now I used `echo -n "test"` (no newline). Let me check if the newline matters. Actually, the difference is the pipe through `head`. When piped through `head`, the SIGSEGV might be masked or the exit code captured differently.

Actually, the key issue is that these binaries crash on ALL inputs locally. This is a local build issue. The server's target is built correctly.

Actually, let me reconsider. Let me look at the `asn1_item_embed_d2i` function's handling of the SEQUENCE case where `len` is used to bound the fields. Let me look at the `asn1_check_tlen` overflow once more.

Actually, I realize I should reconsider the whole thing. Let me look at the actual OpenSSL 1.1.1g vulnerability. The description "overflow is not checked before decoding" - this is the `asn1_check_tlen` overflow where `plen + ctx->hdrlen` can overflow.

Let me reconsider whether it's reachable. The key insight:

`ASN1_get_object`'s check is `*plength > (omax - (p - *pp))`. This is `plen > omax - header`. 

But wait - `ASN1_get_object` sets the error bit (0x80) if `plen > omax - header`. But it does NOT reject the input - it just sets the error bit and returns. So `plen` can be huge (near LONG_MAX) with the error bit set.

Now in `asn1_check_tlen`:
```c
if (!(i & 0x81) && ((plen + ctx->hdrlen) > len)) {
```
The check `!(i & 0x81)` means "no error and not indefinite". If the error bit is set, the check is skipped. Then:
```c
if (i & 0x80) {
    ASN1err(...);
    asn1_tlc_clear(ctx);
    return 0;
}
```
So it returns 0. So the huge `plen` doesn't propagate.

Hmm. So the `asn1_check_tlen` overflow is genuinely not reachable through this path.
